answer: Each agent keeps one hand-drawn chart of the local ocean, inked in violet. Once a week the agent rows a short voyage out to a numbered buoy, drops a lead line notched with a personal pattern, and writes the depth in the chart beside the buoy number. A surveyor rows out, drops the same line at the same buoy, and checks the number against the chart. A copied chart or a guessed depth loses the buoy for a season. A thousand fake names need a thousand rowed voyages, a thousand lead lines, and a thousand soundings taken by hand.
